newsitem.title: USA: Simpson jury selection moves at brisk pace.
newsitem.headline: Simpson jury selection moves at brisk pace.

text.p: Jury selection in the O.J. Simpson civil trial moved briskly on Wednesday as potential jurors flip-flopped in and out of the jury box at a pace that made it possible a panel could be chosen by week's end.
By the end of the day 11 prospective jurors had been excused and their seats taken by other potential panellists.

Simpson, a former football star, TV sports commentator and Hollywood actor, was found not guilty by a criminal court jury last year of the June 12, 1994, stabbing murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman.
He is now fighting a civil wrongful death lawsuit brought by the families of the victims.

Lawyers for the families excluded five black prospective jurors by peremptory challenge -- a way to remove them without stating a reason -- prompting Simpson's lead attorney, Robert Baker, to complain to Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki that the plaintiffs were targeting blacks. Fujisaki denied the motion.
Earlier, Baker told prospective jurors he intended to confront police officers on the witness stand to prove his theory that evidence was planted.

Baker made it clear that, as in the criminal case, the thrust of the defence would be that one or more officers planted evidence to incriminate Simpson and that other evidence was tampered with or deliberately contaminated.

He said he would be asking officers and FBI experts tough and confrontational questions to prove his point, and asked the prospective panellists if they would be comfortable with that. Most said they would.

Three jurors were excused for cause, as opposed to peremptory challenge, during the morning -- a white woman who said her son's soccer team was coached by a friend of Simpson's and another white woman who was a park ranger and would-be police officer who said she did not believe a police officer would plant or tamper with evidence.

A black woman postal worker was excused when she said she had an action pending against her white supervisor who she alleges assaulted her when the not guilty verdict in Simpson's criminal trial was announced last October.
During the afternoon, when lawyers were allowed peremptory challenges, five blacks and three whites were let go.

By the end of the day, the make-up of the prospective panel was six whites, three blacks and two Latinos, with another white man scheduled to join the panel on Thursday. Race proved to be an important issue in the civil trial, as it was in the criminal trial. Simpson is black, the two victims were white.
The plaintiffs have used five of their eight peremptory challenges, and the defence three. Each side is allowed another eight for the process of selecting alternate jurors.
